reason: The text demonstrates that Yahweh explicitly cares for and protects the Hebrew people, not merely the leaders. Yahweh sets apart the land of Goshen where 'My people' (עַמִּי) stand to prevent the plagues from affecting them ('וְהִפְלֵיתִי בַיּוֹם הַהוּא את ארץ גשן...לבלתי היות שם עָרֹב'). The text states 'וּלְכָל־ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם' - all the Israelite people have light in their dwellings during the darkness plague. Yahweh's instructions to Moses and Aaron are specifically for the benefit of 'My people' (עַמִּי) whom they are to free from slavery. The entire narrative demonstrates Yahweh's empathy for the Hebrew people through protective and redemptive actions.
